capture_semantics: Hook tensors are immutable selected-row CPU snapshots made by detach().index_select(...).cpu().clone() during the hook; later residual mutation does not alter these saved values.

Decoder boundaries store the two tuple tensors separately: hidden is MLP branch output and residual is the skip stream. The sparse source's label hidden_plus_residual describes conceptual semantics; no sum was saved or used for the primary comparison.

At final RMSNorm, tuple index0 is normalized hidden, tuple index1 is updated residual after adding the last MLP branch. Qwen2Model consumes only index0; this analysis labels norm's second tensor separately.

Captured indices select every row with positions==positions.max(); sampler wrapper asserts logits_indices exactly equal these selected rows before saving, and all five registered hooks must be present. Nine receipts and successful worker output support this assertion path; logits_indices is not separately saved.

Each runtime request ID's numeric prefix was matched to the private completion request ID; completion source names and exact512prompt token IDs provide A00/A01 identity. Selected row indices are independently consistent with cumulative num_scheduled_tokens minus1.

Selected positions are511(prefill) or512(first decode). Only positions_max and positions_shape are stored, not full positions, query_start_loc or direct input_ids. Consumed input token identity is supported by returned prompt IDs, previous sampled IDs and returned generated prefix, and is explicitly not a direct model-input capture.
Current sparse source hash is recorded for review; the source file itself is not imported or executed during this CPU analysis. Only worker has a recorded executed-file identity hash available here.

findings.claim: For matched A00/A01 last-query rows and identical evidenced token histories, the first differing sampled boundary is layer0 output hidden in this altered eager path. This brackets the observed difference after embedding and by the end of decoder0. It does not identify an operation inside decoder0, the earliest token/KV difference, or native compiled behavior.

metric_definitions.bitwise_unequal_count: BF16 int16 storage patterns compared exactly,2048 elements per request/component.
metric_definitions.numeric_unequal_count: BF16 numeric != separately reported; handles possible signed-zero bit differences distinctly.
metric_definitions.abs_median: 0.5 quantile with midpoint interpolation over finite absolute differences, including zeros.
metric_definitions.finite_handling: Finite/nonfinite counts reported per capture and per comparison; all captured tensors in this dataset were finite.
metric_definitions.sum_semantics: No hidden+residual derived sum or logprob reconstruction was used.

limitations: No internal QKV/attention/MLP sub-boundaries were captured; layer0 output differs but the responsible operation is unlocalized.
Only the last query row per request was sampled. Earlier-token or previous-prefill KV differences may propagate into the first decode observation.
Single altered eager capture per input/batch condition; N1/N2 prefill equality is an internal repeat check, not a statistical repeatability study.
CPU copies and hooks synchronize/change timing; compilation and graph replay are disabled. No native causal equivalence or native timing conclusion follows.
No raw logits tensor, logprob or probability was saved here; sampled token equality does not imply equal logits/probabilities.
Runtime prompt token identity and sampled history match, but full model input_ids/positions/query_start_loc snapshots were not saved; preserved explicit mapping evidence is described above.
Large tensors stay in .private/NUMERIC/boundaries; public output includes hashes, shapes and aggregate comparisons only.
